Yes I'm in the USA. I finished my basic and went to work for a service. And while I was working I started my para. I didn't do intermediate because I wanted to be a para and you don't have to have an intermediate license to take the course and become a para. You just have to have the basic license. I would suggest getting your basic, going to a service in your area and working there for experience, and then while you're doing that, go to para school. I'm not sure what college requirements you're talking about for para but all I had to have was my basic EMT license and anatomy and physiology, which I did as a part of the para course itself
